lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The Crop Show is on at this table! Bring one crop you grew yourself, held up high, and the judges will look it over.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: A crop of the spring shows best today. One entry each, mind. Results right away!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The judges have weighed and tasted every crop on the table. Here are this year's results!

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Me? First? I only grew those in pots behind the store!

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Ha! My cucumbers took the ribbon. Grandpa's seeds never lose!

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Forty springs I've grown turnips. They still come out the best, it seems.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Potatoes from the south gardens. Dig deep and leave them be, that's all there is to it.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: No ribbon for you this year, but the judges liked it. Grow a bigger one for next spring!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Second place goes to you. A fine crop, only a hair behind the best one.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Third place for you. Not bad at all for a field that was all weeds a while ago.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: First prize goes to the new farmer! Look at the shine on that. The ribbon is yours.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: My first ribbon... I'll pin it up by the door.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Tonight we judge the biggest catch! Bring one fish to this table, held up so we can see it.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Any fish from any water. One entry each, and we judge it on the spot.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The fish are all laid out under the lanterns. The judges have made up their minds!

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: This old rod still knows every bend of the river. That's my prize.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Sunday mornings at the river pay off. Sorry, farmer, this one's mine.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I won? I caught it with a stick and a bit of string!

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: A loach from my own paddy. Sixty summers I've watched them in the mud. Tonight one paid me back.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Not a prize tonight. The river keeps its big ones for the patient. Try again next summer!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Second place for your fish. It only lost by a fin.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Third place for you. A good catch for a farmer!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The best catch tonight is the farmer's! Everyone, come and look at this one.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: It nearly pulled me into the pond.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: For the Moon Offering we set out the best of the year's animals: an egg, milk or wool. Bring one here.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The finest one goes before the moon tonight. One offering each.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The offerings are set out in the moonlight. The judges have chosen.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I combed that wool all week! I won? Really?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: The store's own hens did it! I brought them up from chicks.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Milk from my neighbour's cow, cream on top. I only carried it here!

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: My hens? They live under the straw shed and lay where they please. I only picked the best one!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: No prize this time. Brush them, feed them, talk to them. Next fall it may be yours.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Second place for your offering. The moon will see it from the next seat.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Third place for you. Your animals are doing well.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Your offering goes before the moon tonight! Your animals must be well loved.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I'll tell them tomorrow. With extra feed.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Before the year turns, we lay the year's best stone at the shrine. Bring one from the mine, held up.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Ore or gem, the brightest one wins. One stone each.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The stones sit by the fire, all shining. The judges have chosen the first stone of the year.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: A customer paid me with this stone in spring. I knew it was lucky.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: I keep the best ore back from the forge for tonight. Every year.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: My shiny pebble from the river won? Really?

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Amber. Found it in the roots of a pine I cut for the kiln. Thought the shrine should have it.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: No prize this year, but the shrine thanks you all the same. Dig deeper next winter!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Second place for your stone. A fine shine on it.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Third place for you. The mountain has been kind to you.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Your stone goes on the shrine step this year! It will bring the whole village luck.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: All that digging was worth it.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: The last strike is in and the mochi is rolled. The judges counted every beat. Here are the results!

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My husband and I won this every winter. Seems my arms still remember the beat.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: A mallet is only a big hammer. I swing one all day long.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: We won? I counted the beats out loud the whole time. Don't tell anyone!

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Dad turned and I pounded! He says I swing like a real farmer now.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: I swing an axe from dawn. A mallet is lighter. Still, good dough, whoever turned it.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: No ribbon this year, but the mochi tastes just as sweet. Keep the beat next winter!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Second place for you! A strong, steady swing.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Third place for you. The dough came out smooth all the same.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: First place goes to the farmer! Hardly a beat dropped all night. The ribbon is yours.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: My arms are shaking. It was worth it.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You kept good time with an old woman. And my fingers are all still here!

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: We did it together! My hands only got scared twice.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Lines up, everyone! The creels have been counted and the fish are back in the pond. Here are the results!

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: A quiet wrist and a patient eye. Same as at the anvil.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The pond knows me, dear. I have fed its carp crusts for fifty years.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: I won? Mr. Hachiro showed me how to wait for the second tug!

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: I only came to sell bait... and then they kept biting!

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Kota said to keep the line still and not talk. I didn't talk at all! Not once!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: No ribbon this time. The fish were shy under such a bright moon. Try again next fall!

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Second place for the farmer! A creel to be proud of.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: Third place for the farmer. A good night's fishing all the same.

lines.speaker: tsuru
lines.text: First place goes to the farmer! The most fish in the pond race. The ribbon is yours.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: My line hardly had time to get wet.
